overall_summary: Space-themed content, specifically focusing on extreme cosmic anomalies and planetary paradoxes, is the dominant driver of views and engagement for FACTVERSE. Conversely, generic psychology and brain-related facts are struggling to gain traction, even when re-uploaded multiple times.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice Will Break Your Brain!' achieved 1,055 views, and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' secured 972 views and 35 likes. These far outperform other categories.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on extreme space facts focusing on physical impossibilities, bizarre weather, or hostile cosmic environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles using sensory juxtaposition like 'Burning Ice' (1,055 views) and 'Supersonic Rubies' (609 views) outperform more standard space facts like 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' (221 views).
winning_patterns.action: Structure titles and hooks around conflicting concepts (e.g., hot ice, dark stars, liquid metal rains) to trigger immediate curiosity.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' was posted multiple times, yielding only 3, 5, and 53 views. 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' generated only 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: Pause production on generic brain/psychology facts unless they can be framed through a highly dramatic, cinematic, or historical mystery lens.

weak_patterns.evidence: Re-uploading 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' multiple times did not result in a viral breakout, consistently flatlining under 60 views.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid direct re-uploads of underperforming concepts; instead, pivot the angle, rewrite the hook, or change the visual style completely.

next_video.concept: The planet WASP-12b, which is actively being stretched into an egg shape and devoured by its parent star.
next_video.opening_direction: Show a highly realistic, cinematic 3D render of an egg-shaped planet glowing with molten heat, being pulled apart by a massive star.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that this planet is not just hot—it is literally being eaten alive, losing 189 quadrillion tons of mass every year, and will be completely gone in a cosmic blink of an eye.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven success of extreme space anomalies, uses a highly visual and tragic cosmic narrative, and fits the optimal 16-21 second duration of our top-performing videos.

experiment: Test a 'What-If' space scenario (e.g., 'What If the Moon Was Made of Dark Matter?') to see if the highly-engaged space audience will cross over into speculative physics, keeping the visual style highly cinematic.
